items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: some of Wagner’s great — but some of his other stuff it’s the same thing.

ctx.x: Yeah, less to work with. It’s — I don’t know — it’s interesting that jazz went that way somehow. Maybe the musicians were reacting to the intensity of like “Giant Steps” and those like — all those chords coming so fast. They says well that’s about as far as we can go with that.

Yeah right. You know that was really an exercise you know, “Giant Steps” was. That’s a hard tune too. But yeah, I mean that’s just an exercise. And even that, in and of itself because it just keeps on going around like that, that gets old to me too after a while. I would rather listen to “Cheek to Cheek” because that to me has a sense of logic, you know, that states a premise, it develops it and puts the capper on it. You know to me I find that a more interesting journey. “Giant Steps,” I mean somebody that knows…
Yeah. You make your living playing usually small combo gigs and solo things?
